papers/paper-17.pdf.subtitle: On the Conditions of Relational Flourishing in a Field of Power
papers/paper-17.pdf.teaser: Can power protect love? This paper argues that power and wealth can guard the conditions under which love occurs but can never produce love itself — a political economy of conditions, never of love. Its summit: a generative relation does not oppose power; it opposes the freezing of power.
papers/paper-17.pdf.background: Across the series, intimate relation has been theorised as a generative-relational process — a coupling of two subjects out of which value is generated rather than extracted. But that account was developed, in effect, in a clearing: it did not confront the plain fact that intimate relation unfolds in a field saturated with asymmetries — of power, knowledge, resource, and need — which can deform, capture, freeze, and on occasion shatter the very generativity the series describes. This is Paper XVII; it confronts power directly. It takes as its object love in a precise sense — the dynamics of the real between two subjects, the part of their bond that circles the unsymbolisable and cannot be counted, traded, or directly managed — and asks how that love fares when it must live inside, and by means of, the calculable order of power.
papers/paper-17.pdf.approach: The paper is polyphonic and proceeds by recruiting a different body of theory to each of three questions arranged in an ascending logic — creation, preservation, liberation. To how love creates a world it brings the generative-relational being (GRB) account, whose affirmative findings it takes as established, adding an etiology of how the world-creating coupling breaks down into estrangement (すれ違い, surechigai) through four causes. To how love is not destroyed by power it reconstructs the theory of international relations, stripping away the realist assumption that the currency of an anarchic field is relative power and recovering IR's deeper object: how opaque subjects, unable to enter one another directly, build trust and order under uncertainty without a central authority. To how love becomes free within history it brings a dialectical historical materialism that holds the determining force of material conditions together with the relative autonomy of the symbolic and affective life they shape. A single methodological commitment binds the three: none of the theories can touch their shared object directly, because the intimate relation is a two-level system — an end (the dynamics of love, a process of the real) served by means (the symbolic order of power, calculable and strategic) that tend intrinsically to damage it. The later chapters turn dynamical and thermodynamic: generative balance and generative asymmetry as two 'summits', dissipative structure, the spiral of return, dormancy, and a constrained praxis.
questions: How does love fare under power, once we stop theorising it in a clearing?
How does love create a world — and how does that world-creating coupling break down into estrangement?
How is love not destroyed by power, when opaque subjects must build trust and order without a central authority?
How does love become free within history, between material conditions and the relative autonomy of symbolic life?
Can the tools of power and wealth produce love, or only protect the conditions under which it occurs?
Is estrangement always a malfunction, or can it be a necessary moment of a living bond?
If power can be neither eliminated nor allowed to solidify, what is the right relation to it?

key_concepts.term: The political economy of conditions (never of love)
key_concepts.gloss: The central claim: power and wealth can protect the conditions under which love occurs, but cannot produce, secure, or even touch the love itself. Strategy serves an end it cannot reach.

At the level of the end stands the dynamics of love, a process of the real that cannot be measured or exchanged; at the level of the means stands the symbolic order of power, calculable and strategic. The means serve the end but tend intrinsically to damage it.
The single variable that crosses both levels, and that decides whether an asymmetry of power becomes generative or frozen (extending the account of trust in Paper XIII).

To pass one another without meeting. In the first instance not a malfunction but a necessary moment of the bond's self-maintenance: a relation at perfect concordance would be at equilibrium, which is to say dead.

An etiology in ascending order of culpability: encoding mismatch (the languages of trust and care differ), the unattributability of prediction error, the arrest of geometric-phase accumulation (the bond stops generating), and the order-problem between opaque subjects.
The two summits: a negative principle (continually counter the freezing of power) and a positive one (a difference of power can itself generate, when it serves the end).

A generative relation does not oppose power as such — power can be neither eliminated nor wholly eliminated — but its solidification; the task is to generate, alongside good value, a continual counter-force.

A relation kept alive far from equilibrium fluctuates and returns; the normative weight rests on the form of return — coming back to exactly where it began (dying) versus coming back lifted (alive) — with dormancy as the inward, gathering phase of the spiral.

claims: The tools of power and wealth can protect the conditions under which love occurs, but cannot produce love itself — a political economy of conditions, never of love.
The intimate relation is a two-level system: an end (the dynamics of love, a process of the real) served by means (the symbolic order of power) that intrinsically tend to damage it.
Trust is the interface crossing both levels, and the variable that decides whether an asymmetry of power becomes generative or frozen.
Estrangement is, in the first instance, not a malfunction but a necessary moment of the bond's self-maintenance; a relation at perfect concordance would be at equilibrium, which is to say dead.
Power can neither eliminate itself nor be eliminated entirely; the only viable course is to generate, alongside good value, a continual counter-force that keeps power from solidifying.

A generative relation does not oppose power; it opposes the freezing of power — the political appearance of an ontological law generativity already obeys, by which desire withholds itself from total symbolisation in order to remain alive.

A praxis under these constraints cannot be a technique for producing intimacy (the attempt to produce it directly decoheres it) but a disciplined tending of conditions along two asymmetrical axes: generating value, and suppressing the freezing of power.
papers/paper-17.pdf.conclusion: Love lives inside a field of power, and by means it cannot afford to mistake for itself. The paper's severe result — that power and wealth reach only the conditions of love, never love itself — reframes every practical question of an intimate life as a question of tending conditions rather than managing the bond. Reconstructed international relations supplies the model of order among opaque subjects without a sovereign; dialectical historical materialism situates the bond between determining conditions and the relative autonomy of affective life; and a thermodynamics of the driven system shows estrangement as fluctuation, return as the bearer of normative weight, and dormancy as gathering rather than failure. The summit is a single principle that is at once political and ontological: a generative relation does not oppose power but its freezing — because desire, generating its symbols, withholds itself from total symbolisation in order to stay alive. The paper closes as a polyphony, not a system, and returns in its envoi to the image with which it began.
contributions: The thesis of a political economy of conditions, never of love — fixing precisely what the means of power and wealth can and cannot do for the end they serve.
A two-level (end/means) model of the intimate relation, with trust as the interface that decides whether asymmetry becomes generative or frozen.
A four-cause etiology of estrangement (encoding mismatch, unattributable prediction error, arrest of phase, the order-problem of opaque subjects), with surechigai as its name.
A reconstruction of international-relations theory for intimacy: order and trust among opaque subjects under anarchy, against the realist primacy of relative power.
The paired principles of generative balance (against the freezing of power) and generative asymmetry (difference of power that generates).
A dissipative-structure account of the living relation — fluctuation, the form of return, and dormancy as the inward phase of the spiral — and a constrained praxis of the two axes.
Extension of Paper XIII (trust), Paper IX (the holonomic criterion), and the political economy of Papers XIV–XVI into an explicit theory of love under power.

outline.gist: Opens with the prelude 'Two Bodies Falling' and states the problem — the series theorised intimacy in a clearing; this paper confronts the field of power head-on, around three questions in an ascending logic of creation, preservation, liberation.
Surveys the ways power deforms, captures, freezes, and shatters a generative bond, and introduces estrangement — passing without meeting — as the signature to be explained.
The most innocent cause: trust and care are encoded in different languages, so two subjects who wish each other only good can still pass without meeting — and misread it as betrayal.

outline.section: 4. The Second Cause: The Unattributability of Prediction Error
outline.gist: When a coupling's predictions fail, the error cannot be cleanly assigned; unattributable prediction error corrodes the bond from within.

outline.section: 5. The Third Cause: The Arrest of Phase
outline.gist: Using the series' geometric apparatus, locates a failure in the value the coupling generates — estrangement as zero-phase adjacency, the bond intact but no longer generating.

outline.section: 6. The Fourth Cause: Opaque Subjects and the Order-Problem
outline.gist: Reconstructs international relations for intimacy: how opaque subjects, unable to enter one another directly, build trust and order under uncertainty without a central authority.

outline.section: 7. Protecting the Unsymbolisable: The Political Economy of Conditions
outline.gist: The paper's hinge: the means of power and wealth can protect the conditions under which love occurs but cannot produce or touch love itself. States the central methodological fact in full.

outline.section: 8. The Inventory of Strategies, and the Teleological Filter
outline.gist: Catalogues the strategies available to a relation under power and filters them by the end they are meant to serve — keeping means subordinate to the love they cannot produce.

outline.section: 9. Generative Balance: Against the Freezing of Power
outline.gist: The negative summit: since power can be neither eliminated nor allowed to solidify, a living relation must generate a continual counter-force against its freezing.

outline.section: 10. Generative Asymmetry: When Difference of Power Generates
outline.gist: The positive summit: a difference of power is not always corrosive — under the right conditions an asymmetry can itself be generative.

outline.section: 11. The Dialectical-Materialist History of Intimate Power
outline.gist: Situates intimate power historically, holding the determining force of material conditions together with the relative autonomy of the symbolic and affective life they shape.

outline.section: 12. Dissipative Structure and the Thermodynamics of Generativity
outline.gist: Reads the living relation as a system driven far from equilibrium: fluctuation is constitutive, and estrangement is its signature rather than its failure.
Distinguishes a return that comes back to where it began (dying) from one that comes back lifted (alive) — the hinge between thermodynamics and dormancy.
Defends the quiet, low-throughput phase of a relation as dormancy — force gathered, not lost — and briefly returns to the opening image.

outline.section: 15. The Praxis of the Two Axes
outline.gist: Asks what two people are to do under the paper's constraint: not a technique for producing intimacy, but a disciplined, asymmetrical tending of conditions — generating value and suppressing the freezing of power.

outline.section: 16. Conclusions: A Polyphony, Not a System
outline.gist: Gathers the argument as a polyphony rather than a closed system, restates the summit principle, and closes with a literary envoi.
